method: Reviewed reuse of prototype trajectories, re-grounded on exact canonical normalized observations and loaded through optional per-country shards.
evidence_rules: Big Count primarily informs popularity/access and never acts as a universal football-strength score.
Structural breaks can move dimensions in opposite directions; discontinuities are preserved rather than smoothed away.
Infrastructure/project starts are not treated as completed outcomes.
International exclusion is not interpreted as disappearance of domestic football culture.
Every annual value remains a project-authored derived estimate.

country_notes.FRO: Artificial turf is a major access/development breakpoint against an already deep football culture; tiny population constrains elite depth.
country_notes.USA: NASL creation and collapse plus MLS relaunch are explicit competition/elite-support discontinuities; development centres and academy structures are separate evidence.
country_notes.ZAF: Apartheid-era exclusion is modelled as governance/international-access disruption, while 1991 unification and 1992 readmission are explicit recovery anchors.
